newsitem.title: UK: Lead price volatility may increase - Roskill.
newsitem.headline: Lead price volatility may increase - Roskill.

text.p: Lead price volatility may increase because of prohibitive recycling costs and environmental restrictions on smelter output, analysts Roskill said.
These factors "will result in market imbalances and artificial squeezes in supply," Roskill's report called The Economics of Lead 1996 said.
Roskill said imports of lead into the Western world were unlikely to rise above current levels.
"We may even see a trend reversal, with the Western world exporting to the CIS and Eastern Europe as their economies stabilise," the report said.
Roskill said substitution is a major threat to lead demand.
It estimated that 70 percent of the world's lead is used in lead-acid batteries, but that intensive research to find substitutes was being carried out.
"Although none are as yet anticipated, the future emergence and commercialisation of a breakthrough in this area could have a drastic effect on lead demand," Roskill said.

While in the medium term lead demand is expected to climb, once it begins to be replaced by substitutes in the key automobile and replacement battery sectors "there will be a long and irreversible decline in the lead price," the report concluded. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057
